The Punjab and Haryana High Court has rightly pushed back against the impulse to treat an accusation as a reason to lock someone up. Justice Sumeet Goel’s point is that pre-arrest bail cannot be cancelled merely because allegations are serious or stolen articles have not been recovered; there must be clear proof that liberty was misused or circumstances changed.

That safeguard matters because pretrial detention punishes people before guilt is established, and people with the fewest resources are least able to withstand that punishment. A fair justice system must demand evidence and protect due process—not allow the force of an accusation to stand in for proof.
